page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.3xlarge is a high-clock-speed instance configuration built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with a sustained clock speed of 3.1 GHz, delivering 6 physical cores and 12 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The system features 35 MB of shared L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI vector instructions.

The hardware configuration provides 96 GB of main memory, presenting a high memory density ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring persistent data to be attached via external block storage volumes. System networking includes a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps. Memory subsystem benchmarks show uncached read speeds of 72.14 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 45.09 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads reach 640.72 GB/sec.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across synthetic compute and operational workloads, with a PassMark CPU score of 13015.26 and Geekbench multi-core score of 6393. The instance processes 11.09 million Redis SET operations per second and handles static web serving at 9.73 GB/sec. Because it lacks dedicated GPU hardware, large language model prompt evaluation is constrained, achieving 17.27 tokens per second on 7B models. The balanced combination of higher base clock frequencies and an expansive memory pool aligns this server with memory-bound workloads, including distributed caches, in-memory databases, multi-threaded software compilation, and backend application tiers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.3xlarge is a compute and memory-capable virtual instance powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. It provides 6 physical cores, 12 dedicated vCPUs, and 96 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio suitable for memory-intensive applications. Architectural capabilities include AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI instruction sets with 35 MB of L3 cache. The instance contains no bundled local storage and connects through a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark testing reflects 72.14 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory reads, 11.09 million Redis SET operations per second, and a PassMark CPU rating of 13015.26. Without discrete GPU accelerators, intensive machine learning tasks are limited, but the sustained core clock frequency and high memory allocation make it suitable for in-memory databases, CI/CD compilation workloads, and business middleware.
